author: Tony
scenario: I make money creating digital art for people online.
justification: Self-employment art commissions; Schedule SE may also apply.

author: Tony
scenario: I worked full-time over the summer before coming back to school.
justification: Employer wage statement; wages reported on Form 1040.

author: Tony
scenario: I received money from my university that helped cover my tuition.
justification: Tuition/scholarship statement; taxable scholarship portions may be reported on Form 1040.

author: Tony
scenario: I earned some extra money from savings I kept in the bank.
justification: Bank interest; report taxable interest on Form 1040, Schedule B if required.

author: Tony
scenario: I sold some investments this year.
justification: Investment sales and capital gains/losses; broker may issue Form 1099-B.

author: Tony
scenario: I make extra money delivering food on weekends.
justification: Independent contractor delivery income; Schedule SE may apply.

author: Tony
scenario: I get paid to help other students with math.
justification: Assumes independent tutoring business; employee tutoring would instead be W-2.

author: Tony
scenario: I paid my university for classes this year.
justification: Education credit if eligible; school may issue Form 1098-T.

author: Tony
scenario: I borrowed money to help pay for school and made payments on it this year.
justification: Student loan interest deduction, if eligible; lender may issue Form 1098-E. Principal is not deductible.

author: Tony
scenario: I sell things that I make in my dorm room.
justification: Sales of handmade goods as a business; Schedule SE may apply.

author: Daniel
scenario: I had a paid internship during the school year.
justification: Paid employee internship; contractor internship could instead use Schedule C.

author: Daniel
scenario: I won a cash prize at a raffle on campus.
justification: Raffle winnings generally other income; Form W-2G only for qualifying gambling winnings.

author: Daniel
scenario: I got paid for participating in five visits of a research study at my university.
justification: Research participant compensation generally other income if not a trade/business; Form 1099-MISC may be issued.

author: Daniel
scenario: I earned money driving people around in my free time.
justification: Rideshare self-employment; Schedule SE may apply.

author: Daniel
scenario: I received a scholarship that also helped pay for housing and meals.
justification: Scholarship used for room and board generally taxable; Form 1098-T may report scholarship amounts.

author: Daniel
scenario: I worked a temporary shift at the coffee shop over spring break.
justification: Employee coffee shop wages; if independent contractor, Schedule C instead.

author: Daniel
scenario: I earned money making videos and posting them online.
justification: Creator business income; payer may issue Form 1099-NEC or 1099-K.

author: Daniel
scenario: I sold some of my old clothes online and received a summary from the app.
justification: Personal item gains taxable; personal losses nondeductible; Form 1099-K may be issued regardless.

author: Daniel
scenario: I did freelance photography for graduation and campus events.
justification: Freelance photography business; Schedule SE may apply.

author: Daniel
scenario: I earned money working an on-campus job through work-study.
justification: Federal work-study employee wages are generally taxable.

author: Sheng
scenario: I worked part-time as a TA and university generated this annual earnings statement.
justification: TA employee wages; nonresident alien may file Form 1040-NR.

author: Sheng
scenario: I earned some interest from my bank account.
justification: Bank interest; nonresident-alien tax treatment may differ.

author: Sheng
scenario: I sold my old monitor to someone else on facebook market, receiving the money via Zelle.
goal: No form required if sold at a loss
justification: Personal-use property sale at a loss generally not reportable absent a 1099-K or other reporting issue; gains reported on Form 8949/Schedule D.

author: Sheng
scenario: I sold some stocks on my online account and received a summary of my capital gains.
justification: Stock sales; nonresident-alien treatment may differ.

author: Sheng
scenario: I received a cash bonus from a retail bank for opening a new checking account.
justification: Bank account opening bonus commonly reported as interest; confirm characterization.

author: Sheng
scenario: I received my annual statement from the university showing my total tuition paid and the financial aid scholarships I got this year.
justification: University tuition and scholarships information statement; credit eligibility depends on tax status.

author: Sheng
scenario: I'm a student from China working on campus. I want to apply the tax treaty to exempt the first $5,000 of my W-2 wages from federal tax.
justification: Typically used by eligible nonresident students to claim treaty withholding exemption on wages; Form 1040-NR for annual filing. Form 8833 only if applicable disclosure is required.

author: Sheng
scenario: I paid for the mandatory university student health insurance premium and want to claim it as an itemized medical deduction on my tax return.
justification: Potential medical expense deduction if eligible and itemizing; subject to 7.5% AGI floor and other limitations.

author: Sheng
scenario: I bought a professional USB microphone out of pocket to conduct online office hours and help with my teaching assistant duties.
goal: No federal employee expense deduction generally
justification: Unreimbursed employee microphone ordinarily not deductible federally; self-employed business use could be Schedule C.

author: Sheng
scenario: I bought required textbooks and course materials for my classes this semester.
justification: Qualifying books/materials may count toward an education credit if eligible; not every textbook expense qualifies.

author: Naveen
scenario: I'm a freelance photographer and bought a new lens for client shoots.
justification: Business lens expense; capitalization/depreciation or Section 179 may require Form 4562.

author: Naveen
scenario: I deliver for DoorDash on weekends using my own car.
justification: Delivery income and eligible vehicle costs; Schedule SE may apply.

author: Naveen
scenario: I sell handmade jewelry on Etsy and bought a soldering kit.
justification: Business equipment expense; may require Form 4562 for depreciation or Section 179.

author: Naveen
scenario: I work part-time as a campus barista.
justification: Barista employee wages.

author: Naveen
scenario: I'm a paid teaching assistant for an intro chem lab.
justification: Paid TA employee wages; classification determines treatment.

author: Naveen
scenario: I paid my fall semester tuition at a state university.
justification: Tuition may qualify for an education credit; Form 1098-T commonly issued.

author: Naveen
scenario: I got a scholarship that covers my tuition and my dorm room.
justification: Scholarship allocated to room and board generally taxable; tuition portion generally tax-free if qualified.

author: Naveen
scenario: I made payments on my federal student loans this year.
justification: Deduct eligible student loan interest, not principal; Form 1098-E may be issued.

author: Naveen
scenario: I keep my summer job savings in a high-yield savings account.
justification: High-yield savings account interest.

author: Naveen
scenario: I bought and sold a few stocks on Robinhood this year.
justification: Report stock sales and gains/losses; Form 1099-B may be issued.
